subject: OrchidCloud v5.2 rollout - latency & quality degradation
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@orchidcloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@orchidcloud.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production p99 spike after v5.2 rollout (urgent)

Vanessa —

We pushed Redwood runtime v5.2 (q8-compressed profile) to 3 of our clusters at 01:00 UTC this morning. Since the deploy we've seen a ~2.6x p99 latency increase for inference requests and a jump in application-level errors (NLG hallucination rate) that is causing downstream failures. Traffic is steady; no obvious spikes on our side.

We need immediate assistance: detailed logs, an explanation of the latency regression, and preferred rollback options. Our users are seeing timeouts and incorrect chargeback descriptions which is now impacting billing reconciliation.

Attaching a small sample of failing requests and a summary chart. Happy to jump on a call.

Attachments: orchid-customer-sample-requests.json, orchid-sample-charts.png

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Sr. Platform Engineer
OrchidCloud
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@orchidcloud.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@orchidcloud.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production p99 spike after v5.2 rollout (urgent)

Alex —

Really sorry you're seeing this. Thank you for the samples and the chart; that's exactly what we need. I've escalated to engineering and CS. Rishi, can you prioritize a triage? We'll assemble logs and a rollback plan within the hour.

In the meantime: 1) please confirm whether you applied any custom prefix-caching or prefix-dropping rules for these clusters, and 2) if you can isolate a small request id that reproduces an incorrect response we can use to validate.

I'll coordinate and follow up with an ETA within 30–45 minutes. If you'd prefer a short bridge, we can do 09:00 UTC.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Lead Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@orchidcloud.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@orchidcloud.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production p99 spike after v5.2 rollout (urgent)

Vanessa / Alex —

Quick summary from triage: preliminary traces indicate that the q8 profile in v5.2 enabled a new kernel path that increases attention recomputation for long-context requests (average sequence length ~920 tokens for OrchidCloud). That path reduces memory but increases per-token compute when KV cache misses occur. On cold starts and sharded requests we've observed higher CPU/GPU conversion overhead and cache flushes that line up with your p99 spikes.

We also see a small but measurable shift in output token probabilities on a micro-benchmark of your sample set which likely explains the hallucination uptick on edge prompts. We're packaging a comparison CSV (orchid-qprofile-comparison.csv) with per-request latency and token-diff scores.

Immediate options:
- Roll back to v5.1 (previous qprofile) on the affected pools — fastest; requires a short maintenance window and will restore prior latency/quality.
- Reconfigure v5.2 to force a different kernel/path for sequences >768 tokens (workaround) — medium effort, ~2–4 hours to validate.
- Patch build to optimize the new kernel for your sequence distribution — target 3+ days.

Recommendation: rollback to v5.1 on the 3 clusters, pause further v5.2 rollouts, and open a short-lived canary with a tuned profile for low-latency long-context requests.

I'll prepare logs and a rollback playbook; sending the OS-level traces and a summarized JIRA now.

—Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: orchid-qprofile-comparison.csv)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@orchidcloud.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production p99 spike after v5.2 rollout (urgent)

Alex —

We're putting together a Mutual Action Plan:
- T+0 (now): rollback approval window (we can do a staged rollback beginning within 45 minutes).
- T+1h: rollback complete on affected clusters; run 1h smoke tests and sanity checks.
- T+4h: customer acceptance tests; confirm p99, error-rate back to baseline.
- T+24h: follow-up with root-cause and next steps (tuning or targeted patch).

We also recognize the business impact; Vanessa, can you advise on a short-term credit/SL remediation for OrchidCloud? They reported billing reconciliation errors.

Alex — please confirm you want us to proceed with rollback now. If you want a brief bridge, I'm available.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: orchid-requested-logs.zip [log bundle, 120MB])
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@orchidcloud.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Exec approval: OrchidCloud rollback & customer remediation

Marissa —

OrchidCloud (ORC-2026-0421) experienced a significant p99 latency regression and increased hallucination rate after v5.2 (q8) rolled out to 3 clusters this morning. Engineering traced the cause to a new kernel execution path that is suboptimal for their long-context workload.

We recommend an immediate rollback to v5.1 for the impacted pools (staged, non-disruptive) plus a goodwill credit equivalent to 10% of this month's bill while we validate and run acceptance tests. Monica will own the MAP and acceptance criteria; Rishi will manage rollback and postmortem.

If you approve, we'll schedule the rollback to start within 30–45 minutes of approval and notify the customer with the timeline.

Proposed approval: rollback + 10% credit + incident postmortem within 72 hours.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Lead Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
(Required: Marissa, please reply with APPROVED/DECLINED and any modification.)
